newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico judge frees four in politician slaying - TV.
newsitem.headline: Mexico judge frees four in politician slaying - TV.

text.p: A Mexican appeals court judge overturned the convictions of four people in the 1994 slaying of top Mexican politician Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu, pro-government TV station Televisa said on Thursday.

The four had been sentenced to up to 34 years in prison for their alleged part in preparations to kill Ruiz, who was secretary-general of the long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) when he was killed by a single gunman Sept. 28, 1994.
One of the four, Maria Eugenia Ramirez Arauz, was raped and tortured during interrogations, officials have admitted.
The other three were named as Ramirez's brother Roberto Angel Ramirez Arauz, Jesus Sanchez and Jose Pascual Alvarez.
None was accused of playing a major role in the murder.
Raul Salinas de Gortari, brother of former Mexican president Carlos Salinas de Gortari, is in jail on charges of ordering the killing.
Court officials could not immediately be contacted to confirm the report.

The release of the four would be another blow for prosecutors who have repeatedly failed to make charges stick in their probes into the killings of Ruiz and of PRI presidential candidate Luis Donaldo Colosio, who was assassinated on March 23, 1994.

President Ernesto Zedillo fired Attorney General Antonio Lozano earlier this month, in what was believed to be a show of frustration at shoddy detective work in the two cases, and named human rights lawyer Jorge Madrazo Cuellar to replace him.
Carlos Salinas, who lives in self-imposed exile in Ireland, is due to be questioned by prosecutors about the Ruiz killing as soon as a new special prosecutor for the case has been appointed.
